newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trading slows down.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trading slows down.

text.p: Shares in Aviation Development Company (ADC) came under pressure on Friday, shedding nearly four percent after its Boeing 727 jet crashed on Thursday.
The share fell 20 kobo to 4.40 naira.
But dealers said trading was generally light on the exchange on Friday.
The all-share index dropped marginally to 6654.50 from 6654.52 on Thursday.
Dealers said they were awaiting further developments on the crash which could affect Nigeria's only quoted aviation firm.

Shares of Union Bank, one of the country's four biggest also fell on speculation that the Nigerian military government may have signed a decree which allows it to hold a "golden share" in the banks. First Bank, Afribank and United Bank of Africa are the other three.
Union Bank shed 10 kobo to close at 7.00 naira.
FSB International Bank and Guaranty Trust Bank both lost five kobo apiece to 4.90 naira and 13.90 naira, respectively.
But Nigerian Breweries gained 20 kobo to record its best trading week in the year, closing at 11.20 naira after investors resumed buying its shares.
African Petroleum on Friday posted a half-year lower net profit by end-June but its shares ended unchanged.
The company said after tax profit fell to 473 million naira from 585 million a year earlier on a turnover of 1.6 billion naira against 1.8 billion in 1995.
Shares of fellow oil marketer Total, Unipetrol and National closed at 50.50, 47.30 and 38.83 naira, up by 35 kobo, 30 kobo and 23 kobo, respectively.
Mobil and Texaco both gained 20 kobo to 43.00 naira and 28.50 naira, respectively. Agip was five kobo up at 15.90 naira.
Insurance firm Law Union and Rock rose 25 kobo to 6.30 naira while AIICO Insurance closed at 8.20 naira, up by five kobo.
Union Dicon Salt and Nestle, both in the food sector, ended 39.40 naira and 40.10 naira, up by 30 and 10 kobo, respectively

The major losers were Cadbury, 10 kobo down to 25.80 naira and First Aluminium, 20 kobo lower at 4.10 naira. Ashaka Cement also fell seven kobo to 19.40 naira while conglomerate UAC, slid by five to 9.20 naira.
